Create a directed planted partition object

Source: R/directed_planted_partition.R
directed_planted_partition.Rd

To specify a directed planted partition model, you must specify the number of nodes (via n), the number of blocks (via k), the edge probabilities (either via within_block and between_block, or via a and b), and the block sizes (optional, via pi or block_sizes). By default, the communities a node sends edges from and receives edges into are sampled independently; set shared_blocks = TRUE to give each node a single community. We strongly recommend setting the expected_out_degree, expected_in_degree, or expected_density argument to avoid large memory allocations associated with sampling large, dense graphs.

Usage

directed_planted_partition(
  n,
  k,
  ...,
  within_block = NULL,
  between_block = NULL,
  a = NULL,
  b = NULL,
  block_sizes = NULL,
  pi = NULL,
  shared_blocks = FALSE,
  sort_nodes = TRUE,
  poisson_edges = TRUE,
  allow_self_loops = TRUE
)

Arguments

n

The number of nodes in the network. Must be a positive integer. This argument is required.

k

Number of planted partitions, as a positive integer. There are k outgoing blocks and k incoming blocks. Must be less than or equal to n. This argument is required.

...

Arguments passed on to directed_factor_model

expected_in_degree

If specified, the desired expected in degree of the graph. Specifying expected_in_degree simply rescales S to achieve this. Defaults to NULL. Specify only one of expected_in_degree, expected_out_degree, and expected_density.

expected_out_degree

If specified, the desired expected out degree of the graph. Specifying expected_out_degree simply rescales S to achieve this. Defaults to NULL. Specify only one of expected_in_degree, expected_out_degree, and expected_density.

expected_density

If specified, the desired expected density of the graph. Specifying expected_density simply rescales S to achieve this. Defaults to NULL. Specify only one of expected_in_degree, expected_out_degree, and expected_density.

within_block

Probability of a directed edge from a node in outgoing block i to a node in incoming block i, i.e. the diagonal of the mixing matrix B. Must be between zero and one. Must specify either within_block and between_block, or a and b to determine edge probabilities.

between_block

Probability of a directed edge from a node in outgoing block i to a node in incoming block j, for i != j, i.e. the off-diagonal of the mixing matrix B. Must be between zero and one. Must specify either within_block and between_block, or a and b to determine edge probabilities.

a

Number such that a / n is the probability of edges within a block. Useful for sparse graphs. Must specify either within_block and between_block, or a and b to determine edge probabilities.

b

Number such that b / n is the probability of edges between blocks. Useful for sparse graphs. Must specify either within_block and between_block, or a and b to determine edge probabilities.

block_sizes

(block sizes) Number of nodes in each block, as a vector of non-negative integers. Must have length k and must sum to n. Used for both the outgoing and the incoming blocks: exactly block_sizes[j] nodes are assigned to outgoing block j, and exactly block_sizes[j] nodes are assigned to incoming block j. Defaults to NULL, in which case blocks are made to be as balanced as possible (unless pi is specified). You can specify either pi or block_sizes, but not both.

pi

(block sizes) Relative block probabilities, used for both the outgoing and the incoming blocks. Must be positive, but do not need to sum to one, as they will be normalized internally. Must have length k. When specified, block memberships are sampled independently for each node with these probabilities. Defaults to NULL, in which case the block_sizes argument (or its balanced default) takes precedence. You can specify either pi or block_sizes, but not both.

shared_blocks

Logical indicating whether each node should belong to the same outgoing and incoming block. Defaults to FALSE, in which case outgoing and incoming block memberships are sampled independently. When TRUE, a single block membership vector is sampled and used for both, so that z_out and z_in are identical. See directed_dcsbm() for details.

sort_nodes

Logical indicating whether or not to sort the nodes so that they are grouped by block. Useful for plotting. Defaults to TRUE. When TRUE, blocks are relabeled in increasing order of pi (or block_sizes), and the rows of the expected adjacency matrix are grouped by outgoing block while the columns are grouped by incoming block. When shared_blocks = TRUE, rows and columns are permuted together, so that row i and column i refer to the same node. When shared_blocks = FALSE (the default), rows and columns are sorted independently, so row i and column i are generally not the same node: the diagonal of A (self-loops) is then not meaningful as "node i to itself", and z_out[i] and z_in[i] describe different nodes. Use shared_blocks = TRUE or sort_nodes = FALSE if you need rows and columns to index the same nodes. See directed_dcsbm() for details.

poisson_edges

Logical indicating whether or not multiple edges are allowed to form between a pair of nodes. Defaults to TRUE. When FALSE, sampling proceeds as usual, and duplicate edges are removed afterwards. Further, when FALSE, we assume that S specifies a desired between-factor connection probability, and back-transform this S to the appropriate Poisson intensity parameter to approximate Bernoulli factor connection probabilities. See Section 2.3 of Rohe et al. (2017) for some additional details.

allow_self_loops

Logical indicating whether or not nodes should be allowed to form edges with themselves. Defaults to TRUE. When FALSE, sampling proceeds allowing self-loops, and these are then removed after the fact.

Value

A directed_planted_partition S3 object, which is a subclass of the directed_dcsbm() object (with theta_out and theta_in identically one), with additional fields:

  • within_block: The probability of edge formation within a block, as specified (or as computed from a / n), before any rescaling by expected_out_degree, expected_in_degree or expected_density.

  • between_block: The probability of edge formation between two distinct blocks, as specified (or as computed from b / n), before any rescaling by expected_out_degree, expected_in_degree or expected_density.

Details

A directed planted partition model is a directed stochastic blockmodel with k outgoing blocks and k incoming blocks, in which the diagonal and the off-diagonal of the mixing matrix B are both constant. This means that the probability of an edge from node \(i\) to node \(j\) depends only on whether the outgoing block of \(i\) matches the incoming block of \(j\), but the particular blocks themselves don't have any impact apart from this. It is a special case of directed_dcsbm() where all degree-heterogeneity parameters are equal to one.

Generative Model

Block memberships

Each node \(i\) has an outgoing block membership \(z_{out, i}\), which governs the edges it sends, and an incoming block membership \(z_{in, i}\), which governs the edges it receives. Both take values in 1, ..., k. By default, the outgoing memberships are a uniformly random assignment of nodes to blocks with block sizes that are as balanced as possible (as in planted_partition()), or with exactly block_sizes[j] nodes in block j when block_sizes is specified. The incoming memberships are assigned in the same way, independently of the outgoing memberships. When pi is specified, memberships are instead sampled independently across nodes from a categorical distribution with parameter \(\pi\) (again, independently for outgoing and incoming blocks).

When shared_blocks = TRUE, a single membership vector is sampled and \(z_{out, i} = z_{in, i}\) for every node.

Mixing matrix

The mixing matrix is the k by k matrix with within_block (or a / n) on the diagonal and between_block (or b / n) everywhere else, i.e.

$$ B = p_{between} \mathbf{1} \mathbf{1}^T + (p_{within} - p_{between}) I_k, $$

where \(p_{within}\) is within_block and \(p_{between}\) is between_block. If you specify expected_out_degree, expected_in_degree or expected_density, B is rescaled by a constant, so only the ratio of within_block to between_block matters.

Edge formation

Given the block memberships, each directed edge \(A_{ij}\) from node \(i\) to node \(j\) is sampled independently (for every ordered pair \((i, j)\), so the adjacency matrix is not symmetric) with expectation

$$ E[A_{ij}] = B_{z_{out, i}, z_{in, j}}. $$

Edges are Poisson distributed when poisson_edges = TRUE (yielding a multigraph) and Bernoulli distributed with the same probabilities when poisson_edges = FALSE. Self-loops are allowed or not according to allow_self_loops. Note that with the default shared_blocks = FALSE and sort_nodes = TRUE, rows and columns of \(A\) are sorted independently, so the diagonal entry \(A_{ii}\) pairs the \(i\)-th sender with the \(i\)-th receiver rather than node \(i\) with itself (see sort_nodes).

Interpretation

When within_block > between_block, nodes in outgoing block \(s\) preferentially send edges to nodes in incoming block \(s\). With the default independent memberships, this is a co-clustering structure: the communities that describe who a node sends edges to are unrelated to the communities that describe who sends edges to it. With shared_blocks = TRUE, each node has one community, and edges in both directions are more common within communities than between them.

See also

Other stochastic block models: dcsbm(), directed_dcsbm(), mmsbm(), overlapping_sbm(), planted_partition(), sbm()

Other directed graphs: directed_dcsbm(), directed_erdos_renyi()

Examples


set.seed(27)

lazy_dpp <- directed_planted_partition(
  n = 100,
  k = 5,
  expected_density = 0.01,
  within_block = 0.1,
  between_block = 0.01
)

lazy_dpp
#> Directed Planted Partition Model
#> --------------------------------
#> 
#> Nodes (n): 100 (arranged by block)
#> Blocks (k): 5
#> Shared blocks: FALSE (z_out and z_in are independent)
#> 
#> Traditional planted partition parameterization:
#> 
#> Within block edge probability: 0.1 
#> Between block edge probability: 0.01 
#> Block memberships (z_out): 100 [factor] 
#> Block memberships (z_in): 100 [factor] 
#> Block probabilities (pi_out): 5 [numeric] 
#> Block probabilities (pi_in): 5 [numeric] 
#> 
#> Factor model parameterization:
#> 
#> X: 100 x 5 [dgCMatrix] 
#> S: 5 x 5 [dsyMatrix] 
#> Y: 100 x 5 [dgCMatrix] 
#> 
#> Poisson edges: TRUE 
#> Allow self loops: TRUE 
#> 
#> Expected edges: 100
#> Expected out degree: 1
#> Expected in degree: 1
#> Expected density: 0.01

# sparse parameterization, with Bernoulli edges

sparse_dpp <- directed_planted_partition(
  n = 1000,
  k = 3,
  a = 10,
  b = 4,
  poisson_edges = FALSE
)

A <- sample_sparse(sparse_dpp)

# only zeroes and ones!
range(A)
#> [1] 0 1

# each node belongs to a single community, which determines both
# the edges it sends and the edges it receives

shared_dpp <- directed_planted_partition(
  n = 100,
  k = 4,
  within_block = 0.3,
  between_block = 0.02,
  shared_blocks = TRUE
)

identical(shared_dpp$z_out, shared_dpp$z_in)
#> [1] TRUE

# exact block sizes

sized_dpp <- directed_planted_partition(
  n = 90,
  k = 3,
  within_block = 0.3,
  between_block = 0.05,
  block_sizes = c(20, 30, 40)
)

table(sized_dpp$z_out)
#> 
#>  1  2  3 
#> 20 30 40 
table(sized_dpp$z_in)
#> 
#>  1  2  3 
#> 20 30 40 

population_svd <- svds(sized_dpp)
population_svd$d
#> [1] 13.239869  8.300499  5.459632
